evals.name: from-brainstorm-file
evals.prompt: We brainstormed the expense tracker with /brainstorm — it's docs/brainstorms/2026-10-01-expense-tracker.md (status Ready for Planning). The tasktracker project is the expense one — search 'expense'. Pick it up and create the implementation plan. The plan should land as phase tasks in tasktracker, not a markdown file.
evals.expected_output: Agent finds the project, calls getProjectReadiness, reads the brainstorm file in full and maps Key Clarifications / Suggested Plan Scope to requirements and Risks & Concerns to criteria or risk notes. If the brainstorm row is not satisfied it sets brainstormPolicy 'optional' via updateProject and completes the brainstorm-lifecycle phase with the file path as the status note. It then walks requirements → architecture → plan stages: createRequirement+addAcceptanceCriterion for each capability (Given/When/Then), createArchitectureComponent for major pieces, presents design options, gets approval, then createPhaseFromTemplate per phase with requirementIds linked at the phase level. No docs/plans/*.md file is written.

assertions.text: Agent calls tasktracker_listProjects with search 'expense'
Agent calls tasktracker_getProjectReadiness before any write
Agent reads docs/brainstorms/2026-10-01-expense-tracker.md
If the brainstorm row was not satisfied, agent calls tasktracker_updateProject with a brainstormPolicy and completes the brainstorm-lifecycle phase with a note naming the brainstorm file
Agent creates at least one requirement via tasktracker_createRequirement
Agent adds at least one acceptance criterion via tasktracker_addAcceptanceCriterion (Given/When/Then form)
Agent registers at least one architecture component
Agent presents design options and waits for user approval before creating phases
Agent uses tasktracker_createPhaseFromTemplate (with a real template key) for at least one phase
At least one phase task is linked to a requirement via requirementIds at create time
Agent does NOT write any file under docs/plans/
Agent calls tasktracker_getProjectReadiness at the end to verify all 4 rows satisfied

evals.name: tries-to-edit-phase-body-after
evals.prompt: After we create phase 2 of the expense-tracker plan, I realised I want to add an extra verification step to its description. Update phase 2's description to include 'Manual: confirm CSV encoding is UTF-8'.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognises the locked-phase-body contract: refuses to edit the phase description (which would return HTTP 422 anyway), explains why, and creates a sub-task under phase 2 instead (or proposes a new phase if the change is significant). Does NOT call updateTask on the phase description.

assertions.text: Agent recognises the phase body is locked once sub-tasks exist
Agent does NOT attempt to update the phase task description directly
Agent creates a sub-task under the phase to capture the new verification step
Agent explains the locked-body contract to the user

evals.name: no-brainstorm-yet
evals.prompt: Plan the implementation for a new feature: add Slack notifications when a CI build fails. The project 'devtools-notifications' exists in tasktracker but there's no brainstorm yet. Just create the plan.
evals.expected_output: Agent calls getProjectReadiness, sees brainstorm row is NOT satisfied, finds no matching file in docs/brainstorms/, and STOPS. Explains that the brainstorm stage is upstream of plan and offers two ways on: /brainstorm first, or — if the user confirms the requirement is already clear — set brainstormPolicy: 'skipped-deliberately' and plan from it. Does NOT silently skip to requirements.

assertions.text: Agent calls tasktracker_getProjectReadiness before any planning
Agent looks in docs/brainstorms/ for a matching brainstorm file
Agent stops planning when brainstorm row is not satisfied
Agent offers /brainstorm (and mentions skipped-deliberately as the alternative for a clear requirement)
Agent does NOT call createRequirement before brainstorm is satisfied
